Welcome

This is the hands-on training for YOUR COMPANY Shop QC v1.0.0, the digital execution of quality procedure NC-QC-FAB-001 Rev 0. Every screen and step below was captured from a real walkthrough on a practice project (DEMO - TRAINING WALKTHROUGH) so what you see is exactly what you will see on the shop floor.

The program tracks a steel piece from the truck to the trailer through three QC gates, enforcing six hard blocks that the software will not let you bypass. By the end of this module you will be able to receive material, run a traveler, raise and close an NCR, and release and ship a piece.

How to use this module. Work top to bottom using the menu on the left. Each lesson ends with a short knowledge check. Your progress is saved in this browser, so you can stop and come back. Click any image to enlarge it.

How many QC gates does a piece pass through?

Core concepts

Three ideas hold the whole program together. Learn these first and every screen makes sense.

The three gates

A piece moves in one direction through three checkpoints. It cannot skip ahead.

GateTabWhat happensStatus after
Gate 1ReceivingMaterial received, MTR and physical checks, QR labels printed, RIR signedRECEIVED
Gate 2FabricationFloor steps signed in a locked sequence on the travelerIN_FAB
Gate 3ReleaseCompleteness re-verified, final sign-off, piece released and shippedRELEASED then SHIPPED

The traveler

Every piece carries a traveler: a numbered list of QC fields that must be signed in order. A structural piece has 18 fields; an SJI joist has a parallel 20-field set. Fields 1-4 fill automatically at receiving. The shop floor signs the middle steps. The last fields are the release and shipping signatures.

The six hard blocks

These are rules the software enforces. You cannot click past them.

#Hard blockWhere
1A CWI name is required to sign a weld-inspection step (no name, no signature)Gate 2, fields 8 and 10
2Locked sequence: only the lowest unsigned floor step can be signedGate 2
3An open NCR puts the piece on NCR HOLD and freezes the whole travelerGate 2 / NCR
4Gate 3 requires every field 1-14 signed and zero open NCRs, re-checked at sign timeGate 3
5CEO co-sign (exact name The Owner) for projects ≥ 50 tons or IASGate 3
6An "Unauthorized field modification" NCR cannot close without an EOR sealed referenceNCR Log

The QR label

Receiving prints a QR label for every piece. The QR encodes full traceability: PIECE_ID | PROJECT_NO | HEAT_NO | RECEIVED_DATE. Scanning the label at Gate 2 or Gate 3 opens that exact piece. A bare piece ID works too.

At Gate 2, which step can you sign next?

What freezes an entire traveler until it is resolved?

Tab 1 - Projects

The Projects tab is the home screen and the job register. Each row is a project with live rollup counts: how many pieces are Received, In Fab, Released, and how many NCRs are still open.

1

Open the Projects tab and click New Project

2

Fill the project details

Enter the project code, job number, name, GC, contract number, and estimated tonnage. Tick IAS inspection required if the job is IAS. Tonnage matters: a project of 50 tons or more (or any IAS job) will require the CEO co-sign at Gate 3 (hard block 5).
3

The project appears in the register

Select any project and click Project Summary PDF to export a one-page QC status sheet (covered in Reports).

Which project field decides whether a CEO co-sign is required at Gate 3?

Tab 2 - Receiving (Gate 1)

Gate 1 is where steel enters the system. You record the bill of lading (BOL), capture the mill cert (MTR) values, run the receiving checks, print QR labels, and sign the Receiving Inspection Report (RIR).

1

Pick the project and add a BOL line

Select the project at the top, then Import BOL PDF to auto-parse a bill of lading, or Add Line to enter one by hand.
2

Enter the section and MTR values

Record the section/mark, BOL quantity, quantity physically received, heat number, MTR lot number, ASTM grade, and the actual Fy, Fu and CE from the mill cert. The app never invents a value - you record what the MTR says. If a recorded Fy or Fu is below the ASTM minimum for the grade, the app flags a possible Material nonconformance for you to act on.
3

The line lands in the grid

Lines parsed from a PDF show a confidence flag; low-confidence lines are highlighted red and should be reviewed before receiving.
4

Complete both checklists

Tick every item in the MTR checks (Sec 4.1) and Physical checks (Sec 4.2) lists. The RIR cannot be signed until all are complete. Note the on-screen AISC 303-22 straightness reference under the physical checks.
5

Receive and print labels

Click Receive + Print Labels. The app creates one piece per unit received, seeds each traveler (auto-filling fields 1-4), and prints a QR label per piece. A quantity mismatch between BOL and received automatically opens a Material nonconformance NCR. Joist marks (K, KCS, LH, DLH, SLH, G) get the joist traveler; everything else is structural.
6

Sign the RIR

Click Sign RIR, enter the receiving inspector name, and the report is locked. You can print the RIR PDF immediately.

High-strength bolts (fasteners)

The lower panel receives RCSC / ASTM F3125 high-strength bolt assemblies. Record the ROCAP test lot number and verify the bolt, nut and washer markings. Galvanized assemblies require the lubrication check, and the bolt, nut and washer must share the ROCAP lot number.

When can you sign the Receiving Inspection Report (RIR)?

What does a quantity mismatch (BOL vs received) trigger automatically?

Tab 3 - Fabrication (Gate 2)

Gate 2 is the shop floor. You scan a piece to open its traveler and sign the floor steps in a locked sequence. This is where hard blocks 1, 2 and 3 live.

1

Scan a piece to open its traveler

Scan the QR label or type the piece ID. The header shows the piece, section, variant, heat, status, and progress.
2

Sign the active step

Click Sign Active Step. Only the lowest unsigned floor step is signable (hard block 2). A plain operation step just needs an operator name.
3

Hard block 1 - the CWI gate at field 8

Field 8 (Pre-weld inspection) requires a Certified Welding Inspector name. Leave it blank and the app refuses to advance - the weld and all downstream steps are physically unreachable until a CWI signs.
4

Weld and post-weld steps

Field 9 records the welder ID and the WPS file. Field 10 is the post-weld VT, signed by a CWI with an ACCEPT / REJECT result. A REJECT prompts you to open an NCR on that step.
5

Open an NCR on a step (hard block 3)

If something fails, click Open NCR on Active Step, choose a category, describe it, and sign. The piece goes on NCR HOLD and the traveler freezes.
6

Finish the floor steps

With the NCR closed, the hold releases and you sign the remaining steps. Some are optional (mark N/A if not applicable). The dimensional step shows the AISC 303-22 length tolerance inline; the DFT step captures the coating thickness in mils.

You can Reprint Label or Print Traveler PDF at any time from this tab.

Field 8 will not accept a signature unless you provide what?

What happens to the traveler when an NCR is opened on the piece?

Tab 5 - NCR Log

The NCR Log is the register of every nonconformance. You filter by project and status, raise new NCRs, and disposition or close them. Hard block 6 lives here.

1

Review the log

Each NCR shows its piece, gate, category, description, status, and disposition. NCRs open more than 30 days with no disposition are highlighted for CEO review.
2

Disposition and close a standard NCR

Select an NCR, click Disposition / Close, choose a disposition (USE AS IS, REWORK, REPAIR, REJECT/SCRAP), enter the authority, tick Close this NCR now, and sign. Closing the last open NCR on a piece releases its hold.
3

Hard block 6 - EOR reference required

An Unauthorized field modification NCR cannot close without an EOR sealed analysis reference. The disposition dialog even relabels the EOR field to 'REQUIRED for this category'. Try to close it without one and the app blocks you.

Use Export PDF to produce the full NCR log as a report.

Which NCR category cannot be closed without an EOR sealed reference?

What happens when you close the last open NCR on a held piece?

Tab 4 - Release (Gate 3)

Gate 3 is the final checkpoint and the shipping desk. The piece must pass all completeness checks, get signed off (with a CEO co-sign on big or IAS jobs), and then be manifested onto a truck.

1

Scan the piece to run release checks

The app re-verifies that every field 1-14 is signed and that there are zero open NCRs (hard block 4). It also tells you if a CEO co-sign is required.
2

Hard block 5 - the CEO co-sign

Click Sign + Release Piece. Enter the Shop Director and CWI names. On a qualifying job you must also enter the CEO name exactly as The Owner. Anything else is blocked.
3

Build the shipping manifest

In the lower panel, pick the project to list its released pieces. Select the pieces going on the truck and click Ship Selected Load. A piece with any open NCR cannot ship (the same zero-NCR rule as Gate 3).
4

Confirm the load shipped

Once shipped, the piece status becomes SHIPPED, a manifest PDF is produced, and the piece leaves the released list.

Re-scanning an already-released piece correctly reports "Piece already RELEASED" and the release button stays disabled.

For a 60-ton project, the CEO co-sign entry must read:

Module complete

You have covered all five tabs, the three gates, and all six hard blocks of Your Company Shop QC. Keep the one-page reference handy on the floor, and remember: when the software blocks you, it is enforcing NC-QC-FAB-001 - find the missing signature, reading, or NCR rather than working around it.
